conventions.convention: Γ₁G=G, Γ₍q+1₎G=[G,ΓqG], and [a,b]=aba⁻¹b⁻¹. Magnus expansion sends xᵢ to 1+Xᵢ; degree-d truncation retains degrees zero through d.
For I=(i₁,…,iₖ,j), the last index selects the longitude and the preceding indices select its degree-k Magnus coefficient in Fᵣ/Γ₍k+1₎Fᵣ.

Closed-link Δᵇᵢ is the nonnegative gcd of coefficients on proper subsequences of cyclic permutations, with lengths at least two. Empty gcd is zero and Z/0Z=Z. Word lifts at different finite degrees need not be coherent.

The displayed Wirtinger presentation uses compatible common-upper-collar accesses and the source-to-target relation xₜ=xₒ⁻¹xₛxₒ. Independently based meridians are recorded conjugates and are not asserted to generate the full group.

The algorithm uses blackboard parallels in its compatible string-link branch. Arbitrary accesses and parallels require supplied finite transport words and winding integers; the closed preferred longitude removes self-writhe and extra meridian winding.
The Borromean braid product stacks the right factor below the left, so (σ₁⁻¹σ₂)³ is traversed bottom-to-top as σ₂,σ₁⁻¹,σ₂,σ₁⁻¹,σ₂,σ₁⁻¹.
Full AC is assumed for Stallings and the classifying-space branch. Link-homotopy invariance is asserted only for pairwise-distinct indices; repeated-index isotopy invariance remains asserted.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. For a nonempty labeled oriented closed link with a based regular diagram having an underpass on every component, compatible root meridians F=⟨x₁,…,xᵣ⟩, and every q≥2, explicit preferred-longitude lifts lᵢ,q give G/ΓqG ≅ F/⟨⟨ΓqF,[xᵢ,lᵢ,q] (1≤i≤r)⟩⟩. The words can be chosen coherently through each finite degree.

Assume AC. For a nonempty labeled oriented link and every index I of length at least two, any two based meridian-longitude word systems give equal residue candidates under the canonical identification of their residue groups. Finite sequences of self-crossing changes preserve this residue when the entries of I are pairwise distinct.

Assume AC. Both end inclusions of a based r-component string link, r≥1, induce isomorphisms Fᵣ/ΓqFᵣ → π₁(Xτ)/Γqπ₁(Xτ) for every finite q≥1. Arbitrarily independently based positive endpoint meridians also induce these finite-quotient isomorphisms, without identifying the full endpoint group with their free symbol group.
Assume AC. A group homomorphism inducing an isomorphism on integral H₁ and an epimorphism on integral H₂ induces an isomorphism A/ΓnA → B/ΓnB for every finite n≥1.

Assume countable choice. After inserting a type-I curl on every component without an underpass, a finite regular diagram of a nonempty labeled link gives the positive-meridian presentation ⟨x₁,…,xₙ | xₒ⁻¹xₛxₒxₜ⁻¹ at each crossing⟩ ≅ π₁(E_L), using compatible accesses. Any one crossing relator may be omitted.
E(ΓqFᵣ) ⊆ 1+𝔪q for every q≥1. Consequently Magnus expansion through degree d factors through Fᵣ/Γ₍d+1₎Fᵣ and is independent of the representative word.
For the specified based braid (σ₁⁻¹σ₂)³, E(λ₃)=1+X₁X₂−X₂X₁ modulo 𝔪³, so μτ(123)=1. Its closure has all pairwise linking numbers zero and closed-link residue candidate μ̄ᵇ(123)=1.

concerns.concern: Proof 2.1 says, “On the vertices choose based paths joining their values,” then asserts every one-cell boundary loop is null because the induced fundamental-group maps agree. Vertex tracks must be chosen coherently, for example by propagating them along a maximal tree from the fixed basepoint; arbitrary vertex tracks do not have this property. The standard coherent choice closes this short gap without changing the claim.

The title, “Conjugating a longitude changes only lower-order Magnus coefficients,” misdescribes the proved statement. With λ=x₁ and u=x₂, conjugation preserves degree one but changes degree two by X₁X₂−X₂X₁. The statement correctly says coefficient changes are integer combinations of lower-order longitude coefficients; the title should express that dependence.

seams_checked.note: The knot-only theorem was checked against the link theorem. Batch 108 supplies a separate multicomponent cover and proof; it does not infer a link presentation or arbitrary-independent-basing presentation from the knot-only result.

Chosen product tubes, positive normal-disk meridians, and degree-one parallels are preserved. For links, the preferred longitude requires zero self-meridian coordinate, rather than incorrectly requiring its entire exterior homology class to vanish.

Source-to-target crossing exponents agree with the determinant sign convention, and the correction uses self-writhe. The Borromean example applies the two-component linking scan pairwise; its explicit six-crossing sequence has opposite signed crossings for each component pair.

Opened the peripheral definition, exterior-homology lemma, crossing-ball cover, local conjugacy lemma, and longitude-word lemma. Consumers retain the distinction between compatible stem bases and independently conjugated meridians, discharge the normalized-height hypotheses, and preserve the explicit transport and winding corrections.
